newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden denies dummy attack on Russian ship.
newsitem.headline: Sweden denies dummy attack on Russian ship.

text.p: Swedish defence officials vehemently denied on Friday that a Swedish air force jet which crashed into the Baltic Sea was carrying out a dummy attack on a Russian nuclear-powered warship at the time.
Owe Wagermark, information officer at the defence force, rejected Russian suggestions that the Viggen jet was practising an attack on the Pyotr Veliky when it crashed on Wednesday.
"It would never happen that we would practise an attack against a foreign ship or a foreign aircraft," Wagermark told the Swedish news agency TT.
He confirmed that the captain of the Russian ship had written to the Swedish defence force on Thursday over the incident. "There was not a hint of any (mention of a) dummy attack," he said.

The Viggen jet from the F15 squadron at Soderhamn in central Sweden missed the warship by about 200 metres (660 feet) when it ploughed into the Baltic about 120 km (75 miles) from Gotland island off the southeast coast of Sweden.
The 31-year-old pilot, Goran Carlsson, died in the crash.
The head of Sweden's air force Kent Harrskog, said the jet was on a surveillance mission and was trying to avoid a Russian submarine reconnaissance airplane when it crashed.
But the Russian news agency Interfax quoted Igor Kasatonov, first deputy commander of the Russian navy, as saying the pilot had been carrying out a practice attack.
"Such attacks, which have also been carried out on Russian ships in the past, are a violation of all international norms," the agency quoted him as saying.
The head of staff from the F15 squadron, Sven Johnsson, also denied the Russian allegations, saying he did not believe the Russian's version of events.
